full_judgment: 2. The facts, in short, are that the dispute between the parties relates to the land measuring 15.93 acres comprised within Plot Nos. 132 and 134 of a certain Mouza. The said plots were khas land of the ex-rent-receiver, Monoranjan Roy. During the preparation of the record of right under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, hereinafter referred to as the Act, the disputed land was recorded in the khas khatian of the Government. In the year 1975 the respondents, claiming themselves to be in possession of the said land, brought a Miscellaneous Case No. 75 of 1975 under section 143 of the Act in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Mymensingh for correction of the said khatian on the ground that they had become the owners thereof as the successive heirs of Kulsum Bibi who took settlement of the two plots from Monoranjan Roy on the basis of a registered patta dated 29th Bhadra 1324 BS. The said Miscellaneous Case was contested by the Government and opposed the claim of the respondents, contending, inter alia, that taking advantage of the destruction of the office of the District Registrar by fire the respondents had created the alleged patta. Further defence of the Government was that the disputed land had vested in the Government as non-retainable khas land of the ex-rent-receiver and that the government had already leased out the same to several landless persons who had been in possession of the land.
